name: Supported cross-bolt
selection_status: Sole active mechanical hardpoint design, selected by the user. Other designs are historical.
description: Compact printed supported cross-bolt hardpoint with a mini solenoid and a removable payload lug.
load_path: Adapter cross-hole floor → 3 × 3 mm keeper → receiver roofs on both sides of the lug when retained → host mount. P14 anchors the proximal roof on both sides of the keeper channel. The adapter governs the two analyzed straight-pull support states (distal engaged and distal ineffective); this does not establish capacity throughout withdrawal or for the actual aircraft mounting.
why_consider: Four printed parts and one purchased mini solenoid. An integral receiver bridge supports the keeper on both sides of the retained payload lug.
main_risk: The 1.4 mm lug, 0.6 mm distal engagement, actual actuator force, print quality and loaded release remain unverified. Two idealized support states do not establish performance throughout withdrawal.

manufacturing.material: Bambu PAHT-CF is the planned P14 bench-prototype material. Use the supplied P14 print orientations, nominal 100% infill/solid equivalent, and docs/print-requirements.md. PLA remains the analysis baseline; a PLA fit print does not validate PAHT-CF strength. Slicer paths and actual print quality remain unverified.
manufacturing.qualification: No measured working-load rating, coupon strength, loaded release reliability, creep or thermal duty established.

local_control: Off-board local 5 V pulse driver and two-button controller. No payload power/data transfer and no direct RC requirement.
evidence: P14 CAD and sampled rigid-motion checks, plus linear isotropic component stress screens. The PAHT-CF estimate scales PLA strength thresholds by 47/31; it is not a direct anisotropic PAHT-CF analysis. The receiver uses ideal continuous full backing. No physical part, coupon or complete loaded release has been tested; no working-load rating is assigned.

current_requirements.mass_scope: Payload, removable adapter and all hardware carried away with it; excludes the aircraft-side receiver and actuator.

current_analysis.fixture: Ideal continuous full receiver backing; installation fasteners and airframe compliance are not represented by this screen.
current_analysis.method: Linear isotropic component stress screens; PAHT-CF estimate scales PLA thresholds by 47/31. The divided value is an arithmetic comparison only, not a validated working-load limit.

notes: Selected N2 P14 prototype: bridged proximal roof, relocated keeper linkage, flat keeper underside and narrower armature stem slot.
Four printed parts, one Adafruit 2776, two M2 x 16 screws and two M2 nuts; host and payload mounting hardware remain installation-specific.

Distal support disengages after about 0.6 mm of keeper travel, before nominal lug clearance at about 2.3 mm. The adapter governs the two analyzed straight-pull support states; intermediate contacts and loaded withdrawal are unverified.
The 1.4 mm lug thickness and 0.6 mm support engagement are critical print/fit features.
Feed the keeper from +X before lowering the complete actuator; do not force it through the roof.
The integral tab is for ground inspection and manual reset. Remove the force-test hook before operation and protect against unintended tab movement.
The actuator moves the keeper +X. The adapter needs an external +Z force to depart; there is no ejector or payload-clear sensor.
Supplier-exterior actuator, fastener and spring models include explanatory simplifications. Measure purchased hardware and print fits.
The current manifest/viewer describes P14. Earlier P6/P11 metadata and geometry remain traceable in Git history and the archived import package.

33.68 N is the current material-scaled stress screen and 16.84 N is that value divided by SF 2. Neither is a measured breaking load or working-load rating; the provisional requirement is 8.9 N design load with a 17.8 N sacrificial qualification test target.
